question.text: When is a school bus endorsement needed?

answer.text: A school bus (S) endorsement is needed to carry students between home, school and school-sponsored events in any vehicle built for more than ten passengers.

teaching.text: The rule depends on both the trip, carrying students, and the vehicle, one built for more than ten passengers. Remember: students plus big vehicle.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A school bus (S) endorsement is needed to carry students between home, school and school-sponsored events in any vehicle built for more than ten passengers.

question.text: Who can receive a school bus endorsement?

answer.text: Only drivers who are at least twenty-one and already carry either a Class E for-hire license or a commercial license bearing the Passenger (P) endorsement can receive the school bus endorsement.

teaching.text: Age alone is not enough; the driver also needs a Class E for-hire license or a commercial Passenger endorsement. Remember: twenty-one plus, E or P.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Only drivers who are at least twenty-one and already carry either a Class E for-hire license or a commercial license bearing the Passenger (P) endorsement can receive the school bus endorsement.

question.text: What can happen to a school bus endorsement after a failed drug or alcohol test under school bus law?

answer.text: Failing a drug, alcohol or chemical test given under school bus law can suspend the school bus endorsement for one year.

teaching.text: A school bus driver is trusted with many children, so a failed drug or alcohol test can cost the endorsement for a year. Remember: fail the test, lose a year.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Failing a drug, alcohol or chemical test given under school bus law can suspend the school bus endorsement for one year.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: fail the test, lose a year

question.text: What must a school bus endorsement holder aged seventy-five or older do to keep it?

answer.text: A school bus endorsement holder aged seventy-five or older must pass school bus skills testing every two years to keep it.

teaching.text: Older school bus drivers keep the endorsement by proving their skills on a regular schedule. Remember: skills test every two years.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A school bus endorsement holder aged seventy-five or older must pass school bus skills testing every two years to keep it.

question.text: What tests are needed to add a motorcycle endorsement?

answer.text: Adding the motorcycle (M) endorsement to an existing license takes the motorcycle written test, vision and road sign tests, and a skills test on a motorcycle or motortricycle.

teaching.text: Riding is a different skill from driving a car, so the motorcycle endorsement has its own written and skills tests. Remember: written, vision, signs, skills.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Adding the motorcycle (M) endorsement to an existing license takes the motorcycle written test, vision and road sign tests, and a skills test on a motorcycle or motortricycle.

question.text: Which drivers can get endorsements other than school bus and motorcycle?

answer.text: Endorsements beyond school bus and motorcycle are available only to holders of a commercial driver license or commercial learner's permit.

teaching.text: For a Class F driver, only the school bus and motorcycle endorsements are available; the rest are commercial. Remember: commercial holders only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Endorsements beyond school bus and motorcycle are available only to holders of a commercial driver license or commercial learner's permit.

question.text: Where is a renewal reminder mailed, and which permits get none?

answer.text: The Department mails a renewal reminder to the mailing address on your record, but none is sent for a temporary instruction permit or a commercial learner's permit.

teaching.text: Holders of the two permits named get no reminder, so they must track their own dates. Remember: reminder to your address.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Department mails a renewal reminder to the mailing address on your record, but none is sent for a temporary instruction permit or a commercial learner's permit.

question.text: How can you update the address your renewal reminder goes to?

answer.text: After moving, you can update the address that renewal reminders go to at a local license office or online.

teaching.text: Keeping your address current is the easiest way to make sure a reminder actually reaches you. Remember: office or online.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After moving, you can update the address that renewal reminders go to at a local license office or online.

question.text: How early may you renew, and which tests come with every renewal?

answer.text: You may renew up to six months before the license expires, and every renewal includes the vision and road sign tests.

teaching.text: Use the six-month window so your license never lapses, and expect the vision and road sign tests each time. Remember: six months early, two tests.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You may renew up to six months before the license expires, and every renewal includes the vision and road sign tests.

question.text: Whose duty is it to renew on time, and what if you drive on a lapsed license?

answer.text: Renewing on time is your own duty even if no reminder arrives, and driving on a lapsed license can earn a ticket for driving without a valid license.

teaching.text: A reminder is a courtesy; renewing on time stays your responsibility whether or not one arrives. Remember: no reminder, no excuse.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Renewing on time is your own duty even if no reminder arrives, and driving on a lapsed license can earn a ticket for driving without a valid license.

question.text: What can a license office do if you will be away for a long time?

answer.text: If you will be away from the state or country for a long period, a license office can grant an early renewal.

teaching.text: Plan ahead before a long trip abroad or out of state, so your license does not expire while you are away. Remember: away long, renew early.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you will be away from the state or country for a long period, a license office can grant an early renewal.

question.text: How long can a Missouri license be valid, and may you drive once it expires?

answer.text: A Missouri driver license can be valid for as long as six years, and once it expires you may not drive.

teaching.text: Once the license expires you may not drive, so renew before the date, not after. Remember: six years max.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Missouri driver license can be valid for as long as six years, and once it expires you may not drive.

question.text: When may license and registration renewals be handled in one visit?

answer.text: When the driver license and vehicle registration renewal dates fall within six months of each other, both renewals may be handled in one visit.

teaching.text: When the two dates are close, one visit can take care of both renewals. Remember: two renewals, one trip.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When the driver license and vehicle registration renewal dates fall within six months of each other, both renewals may be handled in one visit.

question.text: What happens if you renew more than six months after expiration?

answer.text: Missing the renewal by more than six months (one hundred eighty-four days) after expiration means retaking the written and driving tests on top of the vision and road sign tests.

teaching.text: A long lapse brings back the tests you passed before, so renew well before that line. Remember: late, retake everything.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Missing the renewal by more than six months (one hundred eighty-four days) after expiration means retaking the written and driving tests on top of the vision and road sign tests.

question.text: How many days does the guide count as six months for a lapsed license?

answer.text: For a license that has lapsed, the guide counts six months as one hundred eighty-four days before the written and driving tests come back.

teaching.text: This is the lapsed-license count; the permit holding period uses a different day count. Remember: one eighty-four lapse.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For a license that has lapsed, the guide counts six months as one hundred eighty-four days before the written and driving tests come back.

question.text: How long do service members have to renew without re-examination after returning?

answer.text: Service members whose license expired while out of state can renew without re-examination for up to six months after an honorable discharge or within ninety days of moving back, whichever comes first, but the expired license still cannot be used to drive.

teaching.text: The window lets a returning service member skip re-examination, but driving still waits for the renewal. Remember: discharge or return window.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Service members whose license expired while out of state can renew without re-examination for up to six months after an honorable discharge or within ninety days of moving back, whichever comes first, but the expired license still cannot be used to drive.

question.text: How may armed forces members and dependents renew by mail?

answer.text: Members of the armed forces and their dependents may renew by mail using the Mail-In Driver License Application, Form four thousand three hundred seventeen, with the required documents and fees.

teaching.text: Military families can handle renewal by mail when service keeps them away from Missouri. Remember: mail-in military renewal.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Members of the armed forces and their dependents may renew by mail using the Mail-In Driver License Application, Form four thousand three hundred seventeen, with the required documents and fees.

question.text: How is a lost, stolen or destroyed license replaced?

answer.text: A lost, stolen or destroyed license is replaced with a duplicate, though if it expires within six months you can renew early instead.

teaching.text: If the card would expire soon anyway, an early renewal can replace a duplicate. Remember: duplicate or early renewal.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A lost, stolen or destroyed license is replaced with a duplicate, though if it expires within six months you can renew early instead.

question.text: When can a non-commercial driver renew while suspended or revoked?

answer.text: A non-commercial driver can renew, after the vision and road sign tests, while suspended; during a revocation, renewal is allowed only if the revocation came from refusing a chemical test.

teaching.text: Renewal during a revocation is the narrow exception for refusing a chemical test. Remember: suspended yes, revoked rarely.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A non-commercial driver can renew, after the vision and road sign tests, while suspended; during a revocation, renewal is allowed only if the revocation came from refusing a chemical test.

question.text: When is a renewed license handed back to a suspended driver?

answer.text: A renewed license is not handed back until the reinstatement requirements are met and the driving privilege is restored.

teaching.text: Renewing during a suspension keeps your record current, but you only get the card back after reinstatement. Remember: reinstate, then receive.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A renewed license is not handed back until the reinstatement requirements are met and the driving privilege is restored.

question.text: What does answering yes to the donor question do?

answer.text: Answering yes to the donor question at the counter adds you to the Missouri Organ and Tissue Donor Registry, a first-person consent registry whose decision stands unless you change it and needs no family consent.

teaching.text: Your own yes is the decision that counts; no family consent is needed. Remember: yes means registered.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Answering yes to the donor question at the counter adds you to the Missouri Organ and Tissue Donor Registry, a first-person consent registry whose decision stands unless you change it and needs no family consent.

question.text: What does the optional donor symbol look like, and what does it cost?

answer.text: Choosing the optional donor symbol puts a red heart with a green banner on the front of your permit, license or nondriver ID, and neither the symbol nor registry enrollment costs anything.

teaching.text: The red heart with the green banner is optional and free, and it simply shows your choice on the card. Remember: red heart, green banner.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Choosing the optional donor symbol puts a red heart with a green banner on the front of your permit, license or nondriver ID, and neither the symbol nor registry enrollment costs anything.

question.text: What are you asked after saying yes to the donor registry, and how can you get a sticker?

answer.text: Applicants who say yes to the donor registry are then asked about the optional donor symbol, and a donor sticker for the back of the card can be requested online later.

teaching.text: The symbol is a separate question asked after you join, and a sticker for the back can be ordered online. Remember: symbol question, sticker online.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Applicants who say yes to the donor registry are then asked about the optional donor symbol, and a donor sticker for the back of the card can be requested online later.

question.text: Which donation funds must the clerk ask about?

answer.text: The clerk must ask whether you want to give money to the organ donor fund or the blindness awareness fund.

teaching.text: These donations are voluntary; the clerk is required to ask, but you decide whether to give. Remember: donor or blindness fund.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The clerk must ask whether you want to give money to the organ donor fund or the blindness awareness fund.

question.text: What is the DHH notation, and when must you ask for it?

answer.text: A deaf or hard of hearing applicant may ask for a DHH notation, which must be requested when applying, so emergency and police personnel can quickly recognize the need.

teaching.text: Ask for the notation when you apply, so responders can recognize the need quickly. Remember: ask when applying.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A deaf or hard of hearing applicant may ask for a DHH notation, which must be requested when applying, so emergency and police personnel can quickly recognize the need.

question.text: Who may add a boater safety indicator, and what does it cost?

answer.text: A Missouri resident holding a current Boating Safety Education Card may add a boater safety indicator, which costs one dollar extra the first time it is added.

teaching.text: You need a current Boating Safety Education Card, and a small fee applies the first time. Remember: boating card, small fee.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Missouri resident holding a current Boating Safety Education Card may add a boater safety indicator, which costs one dollar extra the first time it is added.

question.text: What does a permanent disability indicator require, and where does it go?

answer.text: A permanent disability indicator goes on the back of the card only with a Physicians Statement (Form five thousand two hundred ninety-four), costs nothing extra and is never required by law.

teaching.text: The disability indicator goes on the back and needs a Physicians Statement, unlike the medical alert. Remember: back of card, doctor form.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A permanent disability indicator goes on the back of the card only with a Physicians Statement (Form five thousand two hundred ninety-four), costs nothing extra and is never required by law.

question.text: How can a veteran have VETERAN printed on the card?

answer.text: A veteran may have VETERAN printed on the front of the card by showing an accepted discharge document, such as a DD Form two hundred fourteen showing honorable or general under honorable conditions, at no extra cost.

teaching.text: A veteran shows an accepted discharge document to have VETERAN printed on the front for free. Remember: show discharge papers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A veteran may have VETERAN printed on the front of the card by showing an accepted discharge document, such as a DD Form two hundred fourteen showing honorable or general under honorable conditions, at no extra cost.

question.text: What does a medical alert notation require, and where does it appear?

answer.text: A medical alert notation for listed conditions such as diabetes, epilepsy or autism can go on the front of the card with a signed Form five thousand eight hundred thirty-nine, at no extra cost and never by legal requirement.

teaching.text: The medical alert goes on the front with a signed form, unlike the disability indicator on the back. Remember: front of card, signed form.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A medical alert notation for listed conditions such as diabetes, epilepsy or autism can go on the front of the card with a signed Form five thousand eight hundred thirty-nine, at no extra cost and never by legal requirement.

question.text: What does the federal Driver's Privacy Protection Act require of states?

answer.text: The federal Driver's Privacy Protection Act requires states to close personal information in motor vehicle and license records unless state law directs otherwise.

teaching.text: The federal law keeps personal details in license and vehicle records private unless state law says otherwise. Remember: records kept private.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The federal Driver's Privacy Protection Act requires states to close personal information in motor vehicle and license records unless state law directs otherwise.

question.text: What does the clerk ask about voter registration?

answer.text: At the counter the clerk asks whether you are registered to vote at your current address and can generate updated voter registration for your signature.

teaching.text: Updating your voter registration can be done in the same visit, with your signature. Remember: update your voter record.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At the counter the clerk asks whether you are registered to vote at your current address and can generate updated voter registration for your signature.

question.text: Who may register with the Selective Service when applying?

answer.text: Male applicants aged eighteen to twenty-six may register with the Selective Service when they apply for a license or permit.

teaching.text: Young men in the age range can take care of Selective Service registration while applying. Remember: young men may register.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Male applicants aged eighteen to twenty-six may register with the Selective Service when they apply for a license or permit.

question.text: How can a parent stop a minor from holding a license, and how long does it last?

answer.text: A parent or guardian of an applicant under eighteen can file Form four thousand eight hundred eleven asking the Director of Revenue to deny a license, which also cancels a license already held; the denial lasts until age eighteen or until the parent asks to clear it.

teaching.text: Until eighteen, a parent's request can deny or cancel a teen's license. Remember: parent can say no.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A parent or guardian of an applicant under eighteen can file Form four thousand eight hundred eleven asking the Director of Revenue to deny a license, which also cancels a license already held; the denial lasts until age eighteen or until the parent asks to clear it.

question.text: Name grounds for losing a license tied to impairment, crashes and applications.

answer.text: A license can be suspended, revoked or denied for driving under the influence, refusing an alcohol or drug test, leaving a crash scene, not filing an accident report, or lying on a license application.

teaching.text: These grounds involve impaired or dangerous driving and dishonesty on an application. Remember: impaired, fled, lied.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A license can be suspended, revoked or denied for driving under the influence, refusing an alcohol or drug test, leaving a crash scene, not filing an accident report, or lying on a license application.

question.text: Name grounds for losing a license tied to insurance, points, court and support.

answer.text: A license can also be lost for not keeping insurance, too many points, lending your license, skipping court or unpaid tickets, unpaid child support, skipping a required ignition interlock, stealing fuel, a minor possessing liquor, or failing to yield and causing injury or death.

teaching.text: A clean driving record does not protect a license from unpaid support, unpaid tickets or lending the card. Remember: points, payments, possession.

question.text: Name further grounds involving fake licenses, exam requests, felonies and false insurance proof.

answer.text: Altering your license or using someone else's to buy alcohol, ignoring a Driver License Bureau exam request, using a vehicle in a felony or causing a death in a crash, and submitting false proof of insurance are further grounds for losing a license.

question.text: What does Missouri's GDL law require of first-time drivers under eighteen?

answer.text: Missouri's GDL law makes every first-time driver under eighteen hold an instruction permit and drive with a licensed driver, then drive under restrictions on an intermediate license, before a full license.

teaching.text: Each GDL step adds freedom only after the new driver has built experience under supervision. Remember: permit, intermediate, full.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Missouri's GDL law makes every first-time driver under eighteen hold an instruction permit and drive with a licensed driver, then drive under restrictions on an intermediate license, before a full license.

question.text: At what age, with which tests, and for how long is the instruction permit issued?

answer.text: GDL step one, the instruction permit at age fifteen, requires passing the vision, road sign and written tests and is valid up to twelve months depending on document verification.

teaching.text: Three tests open the permit, and its length depends on document verification. Remember: fifteen, three tests.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: GDL step one, the instruction permit at age fifteen, requires passing the vision, road sign and written tests and is valid up to twelve months depending on document verification.

question.text: Who must come to the license office to sign the permit permission statement?

answer.text: A parent, stepparent, legal guardian or certified trainer from a federal residential job training program must come to the license office to sign the permit permission statement.

question.text: Who may ride as the front-seat companion for a permit holder under sixteen?

answer.text: Under sixteen, a permit holder may drive only with a front-seat companion who is a parent, stepparent, grandparent, legal guardian or qualified instructor, or someone at least twenty-five who has been licensed at least three years and has written parent permission.

teaching.text: Before sixteen, an outside companion needs age, experience and written parent permission. Remember: family, instructor, or twenty-five.

question.text: Who may ride as the front-seat companion once a permit holder is sixteen?

answer.text: From age sixteen a permit holder may drive with a front-seat companion who is at least twenty-one and holds a valid license.

teaching.text: From sixteen, the companion only needs to be twenty-one or older with a valid license. Remember: any licensed twenty-one.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: From age sixteen a permit holder may drive with a front-seat companion who is at least twenty-one and holds a valid license.

question.text: How does the companion rule change at age sixteen?

answer.text: Under sixteen, a front-seat companion who is not one of the listed relatives, a guardian or a qualified instructor must be at least twenty-five, licensed three years or more and hold written parent permission, while from sixteen any licensed driver aged twenty-one or older qualifies.

question.text: What must permit drivers and passengers wear, what must be carried, and how is the permit renewed?

answer.text: Permit drivers and all passengers must wear seat belts, the permit itself must be carried because the exam record is not enough, and the permit can be renewed repeatedly without new written tests.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Permit drivers and all passengers must wear seat belts, the permit itself must be carried because the exam record is not enough, and the permit can be renewed repeatedly without new written tests.

question.text: How many hours of driving practice are required during the permit period, and who gives them?

answer.text: The permit period must include forty hours of behind-the-wheel instruction, at least ten of them after dark, given by a parent, stepparent, legal guardian or certified trainer.

teaching.text: Night practice is required because darkness, glare and reduced vision make driving harder. Remember: forty hours, ten dark.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The permit period must include forty hours of behind-the-wheel instruction, at least ten of them after dark, given by a parent, stepparent, legal guardian or certified trainer.

question.text: What may a physically disabled parent or guardian do about behind-the-wheel instruction?

answer.text: If the parent, stepparent, grandparent or guardian is physically disabled, he or she may name up to two people to give the permit holder behind-the-wheel instruction.

teaching.text: A disabled parent can still arrange the practice hours by naming up to two people to help. Remember: name two helpers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If the parent, stepparent, grandparent or guardian is physically disabled, he or she may name up to two people to give the permit holder behind-the-wheel instruction.

question.text: How long must you hold the permit before the intermediate license?

answer.text: To move to the intermediate license you must hold the permit for at least six months (one hundred eighty-two days), counted from the day after it was issued.

teaching.text: The waiting period gives a new driver time to practice before driving alone. Remember: six months held.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To move to the intermediate license you must hold the permit for at least six months (one hundred eighty-two days), counted from the day after it was issued.

question.text: How does the guide count the six months for the intermediate step?

answer.text: The intermediate step counts its six months as one hundred eighty-two days, beginning the day after the permit is issued.

teaching.text: The count starts the day after the permit is issued, not the day you applied. Remember: one eighty-two, day after.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The intermediate step counts its six months as one hundred eighty-two days, beginning the day after the permit is issued.

question.text: What record does the intermediate license require?

answer.text: GDL step two, the intermediate license for ages sixteen to eighteen, requires no alcohol-related convictions in the past twelve months and no traffic convictions in the past six months.

teaching.text: The intermediate check looks back twelve months for alcohol and six months for traffic. Remember: clean twelve and six.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: GDL step two, the intermediate license for ages sixteen to eighteen, requires no alcohol-related convictions in the past twelve months and no traffic convictions in the past six months.

question.text: What must happen at the license office for the intermediate license?

answer.text: An adult from the approved list must come to the license office to confirm the forty hours, and the applicant must pass the driving test and retake the vision, road sign and written tests if earlier results are more than one year old.

teaching.text: The hours must be confirmed in person by an approved adult before the driving test. Remember: adult confirms the hours.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An adult from the approved list must come to the license office to confirm the forty hours, and the applicant must pass the driving test and retake the vision, road sign and written tests if earlier results are more than one year old.

question.text: How many young non-family passengers may an intermediate driver carry in the first six months?

answer.text: In the first six months an intermediate driver may carry no more than one passenger under nineteen who is not immediate family.

teaching.text: The first six months are the strictest, with room for only one young non-family rider. Remember: first six months, one.

question.text: How many young non-family passengers may an intermediate driver carry after the first six months?

question.text: Which passengers count toward the intermediate passenger limits?

answer.text: Both intermediate passenger limits count only riders younger than nineteen who are outside the driver's immediate family.

teaching.text: Family members and riders nineteen or older do not count toward either limit. Remember: under nineteen, not family.

question.text: When may the intermediate passenger limits not apply?

teaching.text: Agricultural work is the named situation where the passenger limits may not apply. Remember: farm work exception.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The intermediate passenger limits may not apply while the license holder is doing agricultural work.

question.text: During which hours may an intermediate driver not drive alone, and what are the exceptions?

answer.text: An intermediate driver may not drive alone from one a.m. to five a.m. unless going to or from a school activity, job or emergency, or riding with a licensed driver twenty-one or older.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An intermediate driver may not drive alone from one a.m. to five a.m. unless going to or from a school activity, job or emergency, or riding with a licensed driver twenty-one or older.

question.text: Who counts as immediate family for the passenger limits?

answer.text: For the passenger limits, immediate family means parents, grandparents, brothers, sisters, stepbrothers, stepsisters, and adopted or foster children living in the driver's household.

teaching.text: Only household family counts as immediate family, so friends and cousins still count toward the limit. Remember: household family only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For the passenger limits, immediate family means parents, grandparents, brothers, sisters, stepbrothers, stepsisters, and adopted or foster children living in the driver's household.

question.text: How long is the intermediate license valid?

answer.text: The intermediate license is valid for up to two years, depending on document verification status.

teaching.text: The intermediate card lasts up to two years, enough time to reach the full license. Remember: intermediate, two years.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The intermediate license is valid for up to two years, depending on document verification status.

question.text: What does the full under-twenty-one license require?

answer.text: GDL step three, the full under-twenty-one license at eighteen, requires a valid intermediate license, no alcohol-related offenses or traffic convictions in the last twelve months, and passing the vision and road sign tests.

teaching.text: A clean twelve months, a valid intermediate license and two tests earn the full license. Remember: clean year, two tests.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: GDL step three, the full under-twenty-one license at eighteen, requires a valid intermediate license, no alcohol-related offenses or traffic convictions in the last twelve months, and passing the vision and road sign tests.

question.text: Over what period are offenses checked for the full under-twenty-one license, and what must not be true when you apply?

answer.text: For the full under-twenty-one license, both alcohol-related offenses and traffic convictions are checked over the last twelve months, and the privilege must not be suspended, revoked or denied when you apply.
